findings.quote: the hill had four stones on it, three cut to one depth by one mason and the fourth set apart by the width of a path
findings.problem: Contradicts a stated place-fact given in the chapter brief itself for the same location.
findings.evidence: book/kharven-year/ch01/brief.md, Continuity section: "Place, from the bible: Kharven-Seat: ... the upper burying ground with four stones cut to one depth." The draft instead gives three stones matched in depth and a fourth deliberately set apart and smaller — which matches scenes/10_wotr_what_the_ground_was_owed.md lines 213/227 ("the mason had matched the depth of the lettering across all three"; "the fourth stone, which was set apart from the other three by the width of a path, and which was smaller") but not the bible line quoted in the brief. Two sources handed to the writer in the same brief disagree, and the draft sides with one without flagging it as a live contradiction (notes_r1.md notes it only as "Bible line for Isaac to correct," i.e. unresolved, not entered).
findings.fix: Per CLAUDE.md this is a cross-source conflict to record, not silently resolve: log a CONFLICTS.md row (bible.md's grave-stone line vs. scene 10) rather than leaving it as a one-line aside in author notes.

findings.quote: He held that chair by right of a forfeiture he had made at nine years old in the mud of the Brine crossing
findings.problem: The archive's own timeline leaves the five-year gap between Miku's forfeiture (age nine) and the chapter's present (age fourteen) doubtful rather than confirmed.
findings.evidence: scenes/10_wotr_what_the_ground_was_owed.md dates the Tenrai refugee wave that brought Miku to the Brine crossing to "over the sixth and seventh months" of "the year after," then moves through only a few more same-year-reading beats (Bram/Vresk Dokkan in "the tenth month," an undated "first frost") before "And in the spring... the instrument was drawn" — a sequence that reads as under a year, not the five years a nine-to-fourteen gap needs. The draft reproduces both ages exactly as the source states them ("a fourteen-year-old boy... forfeiture he made at nine years old", scene 10 line 339), so this isn't an error the draft introduced, and notes_r1.md already flags it ("Conflict for CONFLICTS.md if it is not already there") as unresolved.
findings.fix: No draft change indicated — confirm the item is actually entered in CONFLICTS.md, since notes_r1.md only proposed it.

findings.quote: I wrote the first order myself, and the date is on it in my hand, and I have known since the day I wrote it that a Hallenfeld would one day read it.
findings.problem: Head-hop: this italic is Lambert's own first-person interior thought, not Sodoku's. It follows a paragraph entirely about Lambert's body (his hands going behind his back) and uses 'I' for events only Lambert could narrate (that he personally wrote and dated the first Vaultmere order and has privately known since that day a Hallenfeld would read it). Sodoku is the sole POV; he never perceives this, is never told it on the page, and brief blank 2 (knows / wrongly believes / reader knows) never declares it as something the reader learns that the POV does not.
findings.evidence: R35-2-NARRATION_DISTANCE_ASSIGNMENTS assigns Sodoku Moto 'Close register' and defines that register (R35-1-NARRATION_DISTANCE_BANDS): 'Narration fuses with the character's own idiom. Sustained italicized direct thought is available' — available to the assigned POV, not to NPCs. R4-13-WHERE_SIGNIFICANCE_LIVES: 'Significance may live in a physical tell adjacent to the line, in another character's bodily reaction, or in a governed callback — never in narration itself.' NATALIE.md's older Table Rule 10 ('One italic private thought per NPC per scene') would license an NPC italic in general, but R35-2 is the newer, more specific, same-day-ratified ruling on exactly this question for this POV, and per the index's own convention the newer rule governs the overlap.
findings.fix: Cut the italic. The physical tell already on the page (Lambert's hands going behind his back, in the same order as the seventh month) is a governed callback under R4-13-WHERE_SIGNIFICANCE_LIVES and can carry the beat unglossed, from outside, the way Sodoku is actually able to perceive it.

findings.quote: Edward smells of what he smelled of in the seventh month, when she asked him. I did not know a man could put that back on.
findings.problem: Head-hop into Yoko's private olfactory perception and first-person emotional reaction. Sodoku cannot smell what Yoko smells, cannot access her memory of 'the seventh month' from inside her head, and is never shown learning this on the page. Same undeclared-knowledge-leak pattern as the Lambert italic: the reader is handed Yoko's private read while the POV is not.
findings.evidence: R35-2-NARRATION_DISTANCE_ASSIGNMENTS reserves 'sustained italicized direct thought' to the assigned close-register POV (the roster names Sodoku Moto, not Yoko); the per-character caution for Sodoku is 'no interpretive-summary sentences past Sodoku's procedural read,' with no carve-out anywhere in the ruling for another character's thought.
findings.fix: Cut the italic, or replace with what Sodoku can actually perceive from outside — the sentence just before it already gives this: 'On the bench, Yoko's nose moved. Once, toward Lambert, and back' is a bodily reaction per R4-13-WHERE_SIGNIFICANCE_LIVES and can stand alone, unglossed.

findings.quote: He walks this passage on the outsides of his feet now. He did not in the autumn.
findings.problem: Head-hop into Brida's private diagnostic read of Sodoku's own body. The line delivers a fact about Sodoku (a gait change since autumn) through Brida's unspoken conclusion rather than through anything Sodoku himself notices, feels, or is told — the one channel a sole-POV chapter actually has available for information about his own body.
findings.evidence: R35-1/R35-2 define close register as fusing narration with the POV's own idiom and reserving italicized direct thought to that character; the medium-register definition in the same ruling states the underlying principle plainly: 'POV stays with the character and never head-hops.'
findings.fix: Cut the italic and let Brida say it aloud instead — she already makes the same point in dialogue moments later ('The hands go first. You have that... and I have seen it'), which is the licensed channel (another character's stated observation) rather than her unstated private thought.

findings.quote: Brida Ashwell had worked that out in the winter and was standing in it.
findings.problem: States Brida's private reasoning process ('had worked that out') as settled narrative fact rather than as something Sodoku perceives, infers, or has been told on the page. Nothing shown grounds how the POV would know she specifically deduced his one unescorted route, as opposed to some other explanation (told by a third party, trial and error, habit noticed over time).
findings.evidence: R5-C1-INFO_TRACKED_PER_POV: 'Before a scene, name what this POV knows, what they wrongly believe, and what the reader knows that they do not.' Brief blank 2 tracks what Sodoku knows about the four factors, Yoko's lines, and Tabitha's question, but does not cover this claim about Brida's deduction.
findings.fix: Soften to Sodoku's own inference ('she must have worked that out') or root the certainty in something he's actually observed (she has waited there before, more than once), keeping the claim inside his procedural read rather than reporting her reasoning as settled fact.

findings.quote: It is four leaves, and the clause on the children of the defeated lines runs to a page and a half, and I am not giving a page and a half of that to a clerk with a cold
findings.problem: Possible break of R4-14-CLAUSE_CAP_AT_BEAT [Pack Four Amendment Fourteen]: this is Lambert's line immediately before Sodoku's interrupting value-turn line 'Hallenfeld carries it.' and it carries three coordinating conjunctions (and / and / so), not the one clause the rule allows in the sentences bracketing a turn.
findings.evidence: Rule text: 'Within the three sentences bracketing a value turn, no sentence carries more than one subordinate or coordinate clause.' Counter-consideration: the same passage is also the vehicle for R19-4-REALISTIC_SPEECH's mandated interruption/trailing-off, so the multi-clause build may be load-bearing craft rather than an oversight, and whether 'Hallenfeld carries it.' rises to a McKee-sense value turn (vs. a procedural beat) is itself a judgment call -- flagging as a doubt, not a clear-cut fail.

findings.quote: He was looking at the king's hands.
findings.problem: Possible break of R20-5-ON_THE_PAGE [Naming Guide Amendment Part Five]: Sodoku is close-register POV (R35-2-NARRATION_DISTANCE_ASSIGNMENTS) and is named 'Sodoku'/'he' throughout the draft, but here -- and at its echo near the close, 'was not looking at the king's face' -- the narration titles him 'the king' with no stated reason for the switch, in a POV that is supposed to fuse with his own idiom rather than an outside/institutional one.
findings.evidence: Rule text: 'Introduce a character by whatever name the POV character would use ... the narrator does not switch names without a reason, since a name-switch is a statement about the character's relationship to the reader.' Counter-consideration: the outline's own beat text uses this exact phrase ('watches the king's hands rather than his face'), so the draft may simply be executing the brief rather than originating an unmotivated switch; also arguable this is doing Miku's own framing of Sodoku rather than the POV's self-reference, which the rule's paradigm case does not clearly anticipate.

findings.quote: The Record of the signing carries the witness of each hand
findings.problem: The draft has the Bench of the Accord Divisions maintain a witness-record of a political treaty-signing and send a clerk to demand testimony from a signatory. The wiki's only Bench, the Bench of Attribution, is chartered for a different subject entirely.
findings.evidence: wiki "the Bench" -> Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Bench of Attribution.md: "The Bench of Attribution is not a Division and has never been one... It rules on what a formula is, whether it may lawfully exist in commerce, what class of material a given lot actually contains, and who is permitted to hold the result." Its own subtitle is "Procedure, Precedent, and the Record of Strikings" — a record of alchemical/formula strikings, not of treaty witnesses. Nothing in the card gives this body jurisdiction over political instruments or signing-night testimony.
findings.fix: Already flagged as an open reading question in brief.md's own `wiki Bench` note ("if Isaac means a court of the instrument instead, he says so in a sentence and nothing on the page changes"), so this is a doubt to confirm with Isaac rather than a drafting error — but it should be resolved before ch10/ch12 pay the same hook against the same body.

findings.quote: Ironwood March. The junction. Rimward in nine days if the Cuttings are open
findings.problem: Tabitha's route names an unspecified waypoint "the junction" between the Ironwood March and Rimward. The wiki already uses "the junction" as the fixed epithet for a specific, different place: Bridgemarch, one of Nalūn's seven chain-cities.
findings.evidence: wiki "Vaultmere" -> The Inner World — The Northern Shield/The Kingdom of Nalūn — The Chain-Cities.md: "Bridgemarch *the junction* | The central void, where the tunnel network converges and the largest chain-bridges span two hundred feet across open caverns." Bridgemarch sits deep in the chain-cities, not on the surface road between Kharven's Ironwood March and the frontier city Rimward, so the draft's "junction" is presumably the earlier-mentioned "Hallenfeld junction," not Bridgemarch — but the bare, capitalized "The junction" on the page reuses a proper epithet the wiki has already assigned elsewhere.
findings.fix: Unattested as its own place (the notes already log "the Hallenfeld junction" as originated), but the collision with Bridgemarch's fixed epithet is worth a one-word disambiguation (e.g. "The Hallenfeld junction") so a reader who knows Nalūn doesn't misplace Tabitha underground a chapter early.

findings.quote:
She stopped. "I have never been below ground."

"You will be."
findings.problem: Sodoku originates a fifth line/decision ("You will be.") beyond the four the brief licenses him for this chapter.
findings.evidence: brief.md protocol section: "Sodoku Moto's actions in this chapter... orders the fair copy for Vaultmere; names Tabitha to carry it; says in front of Lambert that the road is hers; answers Brida with 'how's your stack' and goes back to the grain returns. The writer originates no decision for him beyond those."
findings.fix: Cut "You will be." or fold Tabitha's line into narration without a reply, so Sodoku's spoken/decided content stays inside the four licensed actions.
